small_guidance:
- The current ModelNew.forward just calls torch ops — no custom kernel is active. Tuning knobs here won't help; at minimum, replace the conv with a Triton im2col-GEMM since conv3d dominates the 6.82 ms runtime.
- If keeping the torch path as a fallback, fuse div/maxpool/avgpool/bias-add/sum into a single Triton reduction kernel that consumes conv output directly (channels-last layout, one program per N, BLOCK_OC=16, num_warps=4).
- Pre-fold `divisor` into conv weight/bias (weight/=divisor, bias/=divisor) at init to remove the division pass entirely.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite the conv3d as a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM: one program per (N, OC_tile, output-spatial tile), with BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=64/BLOCK_K=32, gathering input offsets implicitly. Conv output is 128×16×14×62×62 ≈ 154M elements — this is the hot path.
- Fuse the entire tail (div → maxpool 2×2×2 → global avg → +bias → sum over channel) into the conv epilogue: each program emits maxpool-reduced partials directly, accumulates them per (N, OC) into a small buffer, then a tiny second kernel does avg+bias+channel-sum. Avoids materializing the 154M-element conv output.
- Alternatively, since output spatial after pool is 7×31×31 and final reduction is scalar-per-batch, structure as one program per (N, pooled-tile) that computes conv on the 2×2×2 input window for all OC, maxpools in registers, accumulates into a per-channel register tile, then atomic-adds the channel-summed scalar to out[n]. Use channels_last for OC-contiguous loads.
